scope: Public Svelte component and pattern exports from ts/src/components/index.ts and ts/src/patterns/index.ts. Utility and type-only exports are intentionally excluded from this batch.

decision.pug_gap_rule: If a migration reveals missing primitive or generic composite behavior, add it to Pug instead of preserving the gap inside a long-lived Underlay wrapper.

candidate_for_pug_when: The surface is domain-neutral and can be named without Underlay portfolio nouns or workflow assumptions.
The surface represents a stable component contract rather than a product page assembly.
The surface is likely to recur across multiple apps and runtime targets.
The surface primarily expresses UI structure, interaction, accessibility, and theming.
keep_in_underlay_when: The surface is primarily a website shell, admin shell, operational flow, or product-oriented page composition.
The surface binds together generic parts with portfolio-specific workflow logic.
The surface carries auth-policy, recovery-flow, or other orchestration assumptions that are not clean design-system contracts.

resolve_via_existing_pug_surface.notes: Use `Pill` with the badge-style appearance. No new Pug component is required.
Use the standard Pug `Button` with `variant="ghost"`. No separate text-button contract is needed.
Use Pug skeleton presets and composition instead of recreating an Underlay-specific wrapper.
Treat save semantics as caller-owned labels and actions over the standard Pug split button.
The metric-tile surface appears to cover the generic metric-card use case without a new Pug contract.
Use `MetricTile` composed in layout primitives rather than minting a dedicated stat-grid surface immediately.
Treat this as checkbox-plus-chip styling composed from existing Pug primitives instead of a new canonical component.
Use Pug layout primitives for grouped field layout rather than minting a dedicated fieldset-grid contract.
Treat as card-plus-layout composition over existing Pug surfaces.
Use the existing detail-row contract or simple composition instead of adding a second detail item surface.
Use the existing detail-section contract with composition for the internal layout rather than minting a second section type.
Use layout primitives plus repeated detail rows instead of a dedicated detail-list contract.
The existing detail-row surface appears sufficient for the generic label-value use case.
Use `ListCard` plus standard slots/composition instead of introducing a dedicated inline-list-card contract.
Treat as list-item composition over existing list/card, checkbox, button, and pill primitives.
Use existing inline layout or toolbar-style composition rather than adding a dedicated action-group contract.
Treat batch confirmation as a caller-owned `AlertDialog` configuration, not a separate Pug component.

resolved_from_pug_review.notes: Folded into Pug Field as the `hint` prop. Progressive-disclosure help text shown via tooltip on the info icon next to the label.
Form-level error display maps to Callout with tone="danger" or FormLayout's error prop. No new Pug surface needed.
Direct replacement. Pug FieldSet provides semantic <fieldset> + <legend> with grid layout. Props: legend, columns, gap, span.

keep_in_underlay_after_assessment.notes: These are better treated as Underlay or app-level helpers for now. They are either framework-oriented behavior wrappers, content-orchestration surfaces, or list/page scaffolding rather than clean design-system contracts.

candidate_to_keep_in_underlay.notes: These currently look more like Underlay- or app-level orchestration surfaces than clean design-system contracts. Keep them out of the first Pug gap batch unless a tighter cross-app contract is written first.

delete.notes: No long-term Underlay ownership intended. Remove or fold into neighboring Pug-backed surfaces during migration.

next_step: Treat `resolve_via_existing_pug_surface` as migration mapping work, not new Pug work. If a new Pug batch opens, scope it only to the field cluster in `promote_to_pug_contract_review`, with `FieldHint` and `FormError` reviewed as `Field` features and `FieldSet` reviewed as a possible grouped-field contract. Leave `keep_in_underlay_after_assessment` and `candidate_to_keep_in_underlay` out of that batch.
